name: Isadora Brennan-Nakagawa
description: The oldest working director in M88's neural-feed tradition, Brennan-Nakagawa made her first BCI-capture film in 2183 when the technology was still experimental and neural performance had no established grammar. Of Irish-Japanese-Haitian descent, now in her late eighties and operating with significant medical chrome supporting cardiac and neurological function, she has outlasted three generations of contemporaries and continues to direct with a precision that younger practitioners find both inspiring and intimidating. Her films are architectural — slow, precise, emotionally devastating — and she has never accepted a studio deal, financing through a network of private patrons she has cultivated for forty years.
cultural_impact: She is the singular figure against whom all neural-feed cinema is measured — the director whose continued existence is both a rebuke to corporate control and a living record of what the medium could have been.
story_hooks: She is making another film — not her last, she insists — and needs a neural-feed capture artist willing to work without a license, because every licensed technician in M88 has been quietly warned off by Vantablack.

Her archive of early neural-feed experiments from the 2180s contains captures of people who did not know they were being recorded, a secret she has carried for forty years and must now decide what to do with.
A Vantablack executive makes a personal visit to offer her a retrospective, full creative control, and complete distribution — an offer so generous it can only be a trap.
